analysis: Examined the head-side test-only file provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift (lines 1-1188). The visible units contain test fixtures and assertions, no production code. The tests cover the T-041 SSD prefix-cache posture: HMAC-keyed lookup tags (keyed per install, salt-scoped, length-prefixed, lines 162-189), DBK3 AAD binding and tamper failure (324-363), legacy DBK2/pre-frozen epoch rejection (233-289), no-follow descriptor-relative I/O against symlinked root/model/fanout paths and rename-to-symlink races (428-619), the production gate where DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE defaults on and one kill switch disables it (627-636), a TTL cap of 1800s that env can only shorten (719-760), disk budget resolver, per-account salt isolation (969-995), corrupt-block fallback to recompute (997-1030), TTL sweep and sliding TTL (1032-1092), and the characterization that read eligibility changes only after the expiry sweep (1094-1167). These assertions are consistent with the documented T-041 mitigations and do not weaken them. The patch excerpt shows later changes (around lines 3441-3545 and 3685-3727) that refactor write-behind admission test helpers. That region is outside the supplied units, and the patch excerpt is truncated, so I could not review it. The only noted nuance is the explicit characterization that TTL is enforced by the sweep rather than at read time; the test file labels this as the existing contract, not a regression. No production behavior or threat-model assumption is changed in the supplied units. The truncated later hunks (write-behind admission/queue caps) are unreviewed and should be checked if they touch production code.
